description: List a company's federal contract awards, task orders and bid protests, with obligated amounts against ceilings. Alpha on public-sector revenue before it is reported.
suggested_questions: List federal contract awards, task orders and bid protests for Palantir Technologies (PLTR) since 2026-01-01, up to 30 rows.
List federal contract awards, task orders and bid protests for Kratos Defense & Security Solutions (KTOS) since 2026-01-01, up to 30 rows.
List federal contract awards, task orders and bid protests for Booz Allen Hamilton (BAH) since 2026-04-01, up to 30 rows.
skill:
Where federal contract data lives:
- USAspending.gov award pages: award ID (PIID), awarding agency and sub-agency, recipient and its UEI, award type,
  action date, period of performance, obligated amount, current and potential total value, and the transaction
  history. Prime awards and sub-awards are separate.
- Department of Defense daily contract announcements (defense.gov/News/Contracts): every award over 7.5 million
  dollars, with contract number, ceiling, location and completion date.
- SAM.gov contract opportunities and award notices; agency press releases; NASA, DHS and VA procurement news.
- GAO bid protest decisions and docket (gao.gov/legal/bid-protests): protester, agency, solicitation, filed date,
  outcome (denied, sustained, dismissed, withdrawn) and decision date. Court of Federal Claims bid protests on
  CourtListener.
- The company's filings: backlog, funded versus unfunded backlog, recompete schedule, and named programmes.

What terms mean:
- Obligated amount is money committed so far. Ceiling (potential total value) is the most the government could spend,
  not guaranteed revenue. An IDIQ award sets a ceiling and is funded through task orders.
- A recompete is the re-award of an expiring contract; losing one removes revenue the company already books.
- A sustained protest can reverse an award; a denied protest confirms it.
- Recipient entities are often subsidiaries with different names; the parent is identified through the UEI parent
  field or the company's subsidiary list (10-K exhibit 21).

Where the alpha is: award-level data appears daily, while the company reports bookings quarterly, often aggregated.

Citations and evidence:
- source_url is one full public https URL: the exact page the value was read on. Never a search results page, an index
  page, an internal file path or a source id. A value from two pages is two values.
- Dates are the date the event happened or the source printed, as YYYY-MM-DD, not today's date.
- Public pages only. Paywalled, logged-in or leaked material, expert-network transcripts and anything marked
  confidential carry MNPI risk and are out of bounds. When only a paywalled article's headline and first lines are
  public, those lines can be used, marked "Headline only:".
- Evidence grades: primary_record (regulator, court, filing, government database, lender schedule, or the live or
  archived page being measured), company_statement, original_press, repeated_press, third_party_tracker. When a page
  repeats a filing, a release or another outlet, the original is the better citation.
- A value nobody published is null. Not an estimate from memory. Analyst opinions, estimates, price targets and
  ratings are views, not evidence.
- Entity drift is the most common error: a namesake, a parent, a subsidiary, a lender or a sister company. Match on
  legal name, ticker, SEC CIK or domain before using a page.

output_schema.description: One row per award, task order, modification or protest.

items.description: One row per award, task order, modification or protest.

award_id.description: Contract number, PIID or GAO B-number as published. Null when the source prints none.

recipient_entity.description: Recipient legal name as on the award.

ceiling_usd.description: Ceiling or potential total value, USD, plain number.

period_end.description: End of the period of performance, YYYY-MM-DD.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.
